tables.title: SAES internal input/output signals
tables.text_helper: Table 402, "SAES internal input/output signals", in section 48.4.2 (SAES internal signals) on page 2305. Columns: Signal name, Signal type, Description. 9 data row(s). Notes: 1. Connected to a set of backup registers in TAMP peripheral that are written, then read/write locked, by the application software (see Section48.4.17 for details).

rows: SAES incoming data DMA single request/acknowledge
SAES processed data DMA single request/acknowledge

Tamper event signal to TAMP (XOR-ed), triggered when an 
unexpected hardware fault occurs. When this signal is 
triggered, SAES automatically clears key registers. A reset 
is required for SAES to be usable again.

256-bit root hardware unique key (nonvolatile, unique per 
device and secret to software), used to internally compute 
the derived hardware unique key (DHUK)

256-bit boot hardware key (BHK) stored in tamper-resistant 
secure backup registers and written by a secure code 
during boot. Once written, this key cannot be read nor 
written by any application until the next product reset.

Static operating ID hardware input used during each DHUK 
computation. Its change causes the erasure of key registers 
and sets the KEIF flag.
notes: 1. Connected to a set of backup registers in TAMP peripheral that are written, then read/write locked, by the application software (see Section48.4.17 for details).
